name: Slack @mention triage
description: When you're @mentioned in any Slack channel, classify the request as 'urgent' or 'background', then either DM you with a one-line summary (urgent) or quietly log it to a memory thread (background).

config.prompt:
A Slack message just mentioned the user. The full event payload is at {{trigger}}. The message body is at {{trigger.content}}.

Classify the message into exactly one of two labels:
- `urgent` — needs the user's attention in the next hour (deadline, blocker, direct ask)
- `background` — informational, ping, or non-blocking discussion

Return ONLY the lowercase label string. No prose, no JSON.
Append a single line to the user's memory under the topic 'slack-background-mentions'. Format: `[{{trigger.sender}}] {{trigger.content}}`. No reply, no notification.

rationale_at_seed: channel_message trigger with contains:"@me" — Phase 2 filter substring is case-insensitive so any casing of the mention fires.
Two-arm chain: classify → condition → (alert | log). condition's op=`eq` is the cleanest predicate for a discrete label.
on_error=continue so a transient classify failure doesn't drop the message — the run still records the inbound event.
alert posts to the user's DM channel (channel_id left empty so seed prompts for it); log writes to memory only.
iteration_cap=3 because both LLM nodes are short prose tasks.
